newsitem.title: USA: Strong U.S. hiring intentions seen in Q3-Manpower.
newsitem.headline: Strong U.S. hiring intentions seen in Q3-Manpower.

text.p: U.S. companies, some of which were unable to find needed employees earlier this year, have indicated the strongest third-quarter hiring intentions since 1988, the temporary help firm Manpower Inc said.

"A very unusual combination of factors is at work in the labor market, underlying the strongest third-quarter hiring intentions since 1988," Mitchell Fromstein, Manpower chief executive, said in a news release.

Of more than 16,000 companies surveyed, 30 percent said they will be searching for additional workers in the third quarter, up from 28 percent the previous quarter and 27 percent last year, Manpower said.

"Much of the present demand is for seasonal workers in such industries as construction and services, but the need for workers is so widespread that there seems to be a carryover demand caused by the inability of companies to find the people they needed in earlier quarters," Fromstein said.
Five percent of those surveyed expect staff cutbacks, 61 percent expect no change and four percent are not certain yet, Manpower said.

Last quarter six percent said they planned cuts, 63 percent expected to remain at current levels and three percent were unsure. A year ago, seven percent anticipated cuts, 63 percent saw no change and three percent were uncertain, Milwaukee-based Manpower said.
Fromstein said all regions of the country expressed hiring intentions not surpassed since 1988-89, but that the job outlook was particularly bright in the Midwest.

In the construction industry, 40 percent plan to hire more workers while just four percent expect to trim down. In durable goods manufacturing, 34 percent intend to increase recruiting and six percent will decrease employment, while in non-durable goods manufacturing, 27 percent plan to increase staff and six percent plan declines.

In transportation and public utilities, 24 percent expect to hire and five percent plan to cut staffing, while in wholesale and retail trades 34 percent plan to add staff, while four percent plan to cut.
The demand in wholesale and retail trades is the highest seen since 1978, except for fourth quarter holiday hiring, Manpower said.

In finance, insurance and real estate, 22 percent expect to add workers and five percent expect to cut back, Manpower said. In education, 22 percent plan recruiting, while 10 percent plan lower staffing.
Twenty-eight percent of service firms plan hiring and five percent plan cutbacks, while in public administration, 28 percent plan to add workers and five percent plan to trim down, Manpower said.
The survey is based on telephone interviews in 487 U.S. cities and has a margin of error of plus or minus two percent.
